prayerExcerpt.en-US: Go into all the world, and proclaim the Gospel.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Ide pelo mundo inteiro e anunciai o Evangelho!

cards.subject: Two early bishops side by side, half-length. Left, Timothy: a white chlamys-like chasuble with a plain white pallium, holding a closed codex of Paul's letters against his chest. Right, Titus: a deep-red chasuble with a white pallium, one hand raised in blessing, the other on a bishop's staff with a simple cross. No mitres. Behind them, Ephesus: the great marble theatre on the hillside and the colonnaded harbour street running down to the sea, with a small ship bound for Crete on the horizon.
cards.face: Timothy (left): a slender young man of about twenty-five with a slim, narrow face and a gently pointed chin — a slender, straight nose, gentle, slightly hooded hazel eyes, thin, faintly arched brows, smooth cheeks and a soft, small mouth; short straight light-brown hair with a soft fringe, a sparse, short, fair-brown beard rounded along the jaw, and a gentle, slightly lowered gaze. Titus (right): a clean-shaven man of about forty-five with a square face — a broad, flat forehead, a short, straight nose with a broad bridge, narrow, deep-set dark eyes under thick straight black brows that nearly meet, flat cheeks, a strong square jaw and a wide, thin-lipped mouth; olive complexion, black hair cut short in a straight Roman fringe with grey at the temples, and a steady, direct gaze. Not a beardless youth, not the thirties man with brown curls.
cards.basis: The Painter's Manual gives Titus as beardless and Timothy (on his Byzantine feast, 22 January) as young with a rounded beard; Titus is made older because he was already Paul's companion at the Jerusalem meeting (Gal 2:1), before Timothy joined him (Acts 16:1), and Timothy's youth is from 1 Tim 4:12.

sources.title: Didron, Manuel d'iconographie chrétienne (1845), pp. 315 (Titus) and 392 (Timothy, 22 January)
Wikimedia Commons, Saint Timothy (icon)
Wikimedia Commons, Fresco of Saint Titos

patronOf.en-US: Apostles of the Slavs, patrons of Europe
patronOf.pt-BR: Apóstolos dos eslavos, padroeiros da Europa

prayerExcerpt.en-US: These are holy men who became friends of God, glorious heralds of divine truth.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Estes são homens santos, que se tornaram amigos de Deus, gloriosos arautos da verdade divina.

cards.subject: Two brothers side by side, half-length, holding between them an unrolled parchment scroll whose writing is only faint, illegible ornamental strokes (no readable letters of any alphabet). Left, Cyril: a monk in a black habit and a black monastic hood covering his head, a small cross on a cord. Right, Methodius: an archbishop in a gold chasuble with a white pallium and a white mitre, holding a Gospel book and a staff with a double-barred cross. Behind them, the green valley of the Morava river in Moravia with wooded hills and a small round stone church.
cards.face: Cyril (left): a thin, pale, scholarly man of about forty with an inverted-triangle face — a tall, broad forehead under the monastic hood narrowing sharply to the chin; a long, slender, slightly hooked nose; large, dark, prominent, intelligent eyes under straight black brows; smooth, flat cheeks; a small, thin mouth; a long, narrow black beard and a calm, inward gaze. Methodius (right): a man of about sixty with a broad, heavy, trapezoid face, wider at the jaw than at the brow — a large nose with a broad, fleshy, rounded tip; small, kind eyes creased at the corners under heavy dark eyebrows; full cheeks; a heavy jaw under the beard; a full mouth; a long, full iron-grey beard with darker streaks and a kindly, fatherly gaze. Methodius's beard is grey, not white.
cards.basis: Eastern and Western tradition (the 1848 Troyan Monastery fresco by Zahari Zograf, Matejko's 1885 painting) shows the younger Cyril with a dark beard and the elder Methodius with a grey or white one; Methodius was the elder brother, and Cyril, the monk, died at about forty-two in Rome in 869.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, Zahari Zograf, Sts. Cyril and Methodius, Troyan Monastery (1848)
Wikimedia Commons, Jan Matejko, Sts. Cyril and Methodius (1885)
Wikipedia, Saints Cyril and Methodius

name.en-US: St. John Baptist de la Salle
name.pt-BR: São João Batista de la Salle

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Raise up, we pray, teachers in your Church ready to devote themselves wholeheartedly to the human and Christian formation of the young.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Suscitai na vossa Igreja educadores que se dediquem de todo o coração à formação humana e cristã da juventude.

cards.subject: A French priest, half-length, in a black soutane and a black mantle with the white two-tailed rabat (bands) at the throat. One hand rests on the shoulder of a small schoolboy in a plain coat who holds an open primer; the other points gently upward. A slate and a book lie on a school desk beside him. Behind him, the city of Reims with the Gothic west front and towers of Reims Cathedral, where he was a canon.
cards.face: A clean-shaven man of about sixty with an oval face and full cheeks — a long, straight nose with a fine ridge, round dark-brown eyes under softly arched brows, a rounded chin with a small dimple and a small, curved mouth in a gentle, kindly half-smile; soft grey hair brushed back and falling to the collar. Not thin or wasted, and the hair grey rather than snow-white.
cards.basis: The official portrait of the Founder, dated 1734 and attributed to Pierre Léger, kept in the Brothers' archives in Rome: clean-shaven, grey hair to the collar, a long nose, a gentle expression, the black habit with the white rabat.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, portrait of Jean-Baptiste de La Salle (after Pierre Léger)
Archives lasalliennes, Portraits de saint Jean-Baptiste de La Salle
Wikipedia, Jean-Baptiste de La Salle (patron of teachers, 1950)

patronOf.en-US: Foundress of the Missionaries of Charity

prayerExcerpt.en-US: To serve Christ in our afflicted brothers and sisters.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Servir a Cristo em nossos irmãos aflitos.

cards.subject: A small, elderly nun, half-length, in a white cotton sari bordered with three blue stripes (one broad, two narrow), draped over her head and shoulders, a small wooden crucifix pinned at her left shoulder and a rosary in her joined hands. Beside her, a small sick child wrapped in a white cloth rests against her arm. Behind her, Kolkata: the Home of the Pure Heart (Nirmal Hriday) at Kalighat, with palms and the river in soft evening light.
cards.face: A small woman of about seventy, slightly stooped, with a small face broad at the cheekbones and tapering to a firm, pointed chin — a strong nose curving slightly downward, deep-set, hooded brown eyes under thin, low brows, prominent cheekbones and a wide, thin-lipped mouth in a warm, gentle smile; the face softly lined with age. Idealise the wrinkles into a few soft lines.
cards.basis: Her photographs from life (the Wikipedia lead photograph): the white sari with blue stripes over the head, the crucifix pinned at the left shoulder, a small lined face with a broad smile.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, Mother Teresa (photograph)
Wikipedia, Mother Teresa (the sari, 1950; Nirmal Hriday, 1952)

prayerExcerpt.en-US: The blessed apostles, then, having founded and built up the Church, committed into the hands of Linus the office of the episcopate.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Os bem-aventurados apóstolos, tendo então fundado e edificado a Igreja, confiaram às mãos de Lino o ofício do episcopado.

cards.excerptSource: St. Irenaeus, Against Heresies III.3.3 (ANF translation, public domain, verbatim), pt-BR rendered from it
cards.subject: An early pope, half-length, without a tiara: a deep-red chasuble and over it a plain white woollen pallium marked with black crosses. He holds a book (the tradition that he wrote the acts of St. Peter) and a martyr's palm. Behind him, his birthplace, Volterra in Etruria: a walled hill town of stone towers above rolling Tuscan hills.
cards.face: A man of about fifty with a broad, hexagonal face — a low, wide forehead and wide, flat cheekbones angling to a broad jaw; a straight, wide nose with a blunt tip; wide-set, round dark eyes under thick, gently arched brows; a rounded chin under the beard; a straight, full mouth; dark hair greying at the temples and receding at the brow, a full, rounded salt-and-pepper beard of medium length, and a steady, gentle gaze. Beard neither white nor tapering.
cards.basis: The Painter's Manual gives Linus, of the Seventy, 'a rounded beard'; the Menologion of Basil II shows him older and balding with a rounded beard. The face takes the rounded beard of both and a middle age between them.

sources.title: Didron, Manuel d'iconographie chrétienne (1845), p. 313 (Linus)
Wikimedia Commons, Menologion of Basil II, portrait of Linus
Divinum Officium, Breviary lesson for St. Linus, 23 September
Irenaeus, Against Heresies III.3 (New Advent)

prayerExcerpt.en-US: We ask that through their merits and prayers, in all things we may be defended by your protecting help.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Por seus méritos e preces concedei-nos sem cessar a vossa proteção.

cards.excerptSource: content/of/order/order-of-mass.json, Roman Canon (Eucharistic Prayer I), Communicantes after the names 'Linus, Cletus' (en-US lines 77-78, pt-BR line 76)
cards.subject: An aged early pope, half-length, without a tiara: a gold chasuble with a plain white pallium marked with black crosses, his right hand raised in blessing, his left holding a simple staff topped with a cross, a martyr's palm at his side. Behind him, the Vatican hill above the Tiber, where he was buried beside St. Peter, with umbrella pines and the Roman skyline.
cards.face: A lean old man of about seventy with a narrow, bony face — a broad, bony forehead, sharp, high cheekbones, a short, sharp, straight nose, small, very bright eyes set close together under bristling, upswept grey brows, a long, jutting chin under the beard and a thin mouth with a long upper lip; close-cropped silver hair, a long silver-grey beard divided into two points at the end, and a kind gaze. Not broad, not rounded, not heavy-set.
cards.basis: The images of Cletus show an old, bearded pope (Palma il Giovane, Venice, 1592-93; the statue at San Cleto, Rome); the forked beard is an artistic choice to keep him apart from the other white-bearded prelates.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, Palma il Giovane, Papa Cleto (1592-93), Gesuiti, Venice
Wikimedia Commons, statue of S. Cleto, San Basilio, Rome
Divinum Officium, Mass and Breviary of Sts. Cletus and Marcellinus, 26 April

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Him who is truly God I worship in mind and in prayer.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Aquele que é verdadeiramente Deus, eu o venero com a mente e com a oração.

cards.excerptSource: Roman Breviary (pre-1960), lesson for St. Chrysogonus, 24 November: 'Ego eum, qui vere est Deus, mente et oratione veneror' (his answer to Diocletian), translated; Divinum Officium horas/Latin/Sancti/11-24o.txt
cards.subject: A Roman officer of high rank, half-length: a bronze cuirass, a crimson military cloak fastened at the shoulder, and a light iron chain hanging from one wrist (his two years in prison). In one hand a folded letter sealed with a cross (his letters to Anastasia), in the other a martyr's palm. Behind him, the lagoon and shore of Aquileia on the Adriatic, where he was beheaded and his body thrown into the sea, with low marshes and a Roman town wall.
cards.face: A man of about forty-five with a compact, square face and a low forehead — a nose with a flattened bridge and a broad tip; narrow, wide-set dark eyes under straight, low brows; wide, flat cheekbones; a strong, wide jaw with a dimpled chin; a thin, firm mouth; close-cropped iron-grey hair, a short, square-trimmed black beard streaked with grey, and a calm, resolute gaze. Clearly older and heavier-built than George and Martin.
cards.basis: Before the 14th century Chrysogonus was shown as a high-ranking Roman officer in cloak and cuirass (christianiconography.info), later as a knight (Giambono, San Trovaso, c. 1444); no source gives his features, so the age and grey are chosen to keep him apart from the young soldier saints.

sources.title: christianiconography.info, St. Chrysogonus
Wikimedia Commons, Michele Giambono, St. Chrysogonus on horseback, San Trovaso
Divinum Officium, Breviary lesson for St. Chrysogonus, 24 November

prayerExcerpt.en-US: The same faith and the same passion made them truly brothers.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: A mesma fé e a mesma paixão os fizeram verdadeiramente irmãos.

cards.excerptSource: Roman Missal (1962), collect of Sts. John and Paul, 26 June: 'quos eadem fides et passio vere fecit esse germanos', translated; Divinum Officium missa/Latin/Sancti/06-26.txt
cards.subject: Two Roman brothers side by side, half-length, officers of the imperial household in white tunics with purple stripes and white mantles fastened at the shoulder, each holding a martyr's palm; the elder, John, also holds a jewelled martyr's crown. Behind them, the Caelian Hill in Rome: the Romanesque bell tower and arcaded porch of the basilica of Sts. John and Paul, built over their house, among cypresses.
cards.face: John (left, the elder): a man of about forty with a broad, heavy-jawed, rectangular face — a thick, straight nose, small dark eyes set close under a heavy, straight brow ridge, flat cheekbones, a wide, squared chin under the beard and a straight, firm mouth; close-cropped black hair, a short, neatly trimmed black beard and a grave, steady gaze. Paul (right): a clean-shaven man of about twenty-eight with a narrower face and a delicate, pointed chin — a small, straight nose, large light-brown eyes under high, arched brows, smooth cheeks and a soft, full mouth; short light-brown hair combed forward in a straight Roman fringe and a gentle expression. John's hair is straight and cropped, not curly.
cards.basis: The mosaic procession of martyrs at Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, Ravenna, shows both as short-haired Roman men in white pallia carrying crowns; the Breviary makes them brothers who served Constantia. The beard and age that separate John from Paul are an artistic choice.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, Sts. John and Paul, Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, Ravenna
Wikipedia, Saints John and Paul
Divinum Officium, Mass of Sts. John and Paul, 26 June

prayerExcerpt.en-US: On the day before he was to suffer, he took bread in his holy and venerable hands.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Na véspera de sua paixão, ele tomou o pão em suas santas e veneráveis mãos.

cards.excerptSource: content/of/order/order-of-mass.json, Roman Canon (Eucharistic Prayer I), institution narrative (en-US lines 106 and 108, pt-BR lines 103 and 105, rubrics omitted); the Roman Breviary lesson for 3 May credits him with adding 'Qui pridie quam pateretur' to the Canon
cards.subject: A young early pope, half-length, without a tiara: white vestments with a plain white pallium marked with black crosses, holding a golden chalice with the Host above it, and a small silver holy-water vessel with an aspergillum beside him (he is credited with the blessing of water with salt). A martyr's palm. Behind him, the Via Nomentana outside Rome, lined with umbrella pines and ancient tombs.
cards.face: A clean-shaven young man of about thirty with a smooth oval face — a long, straight nose running down from the brow on a narrow bridge, large dark almond-shaped eyes under high, arched brows, smooth cheekbones, a small rounded chin and a small, full mouth; short chestnut hair combed forward in a straight fringe, and a serene, open gaze. Straight hair, not curls.
cards.basis: The 8th-century fresco of 'Sanctus Alexander Papa' in Santa Maria Antiqua, Rome: a beardless young pope with short hair, large eyes, a white pallium and a jewelled book. The Breviary lesson gives the Qui pridie and the holy water.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, Sanctus Alexander Papa, Santa Maria Antiqua
Divinum Officium, Breviary lesson for Sts. Alexander, Eventius and Theodulus, 3 May

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Admit us, we beseech you, into their company, not weighing our merits, but granting us your pardon.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Concedei, não por nossos méritos, mas por vossa bondade, o convívio dos Apóstolos e Mártires.

cards.excerptSource: content/of/order/order-of-mass.json, Roman Canon (Eucharistic Prayer I), Nobis quoque, which names 'Agnes, Cecilia, Anastasia' (en-US lines 198-201, pt-BR lines 190-192)
cards.subject: A young Roman noblewoman, half-length, in a moss-green gown with a dark wine-coloured mantle, a string of pearls bound in her hair. In one hand a small glass phial of healing ointment (her Greek title, Deliverer from Potions, and her care for Christians in prison), in the other a martyr's palm; a small flame glows in a bowl at her side for her death by fire. Behind her, Sirmium on the broad river Sava in the Pannonian plain, with Roman walls and poplars.
cards.face: A young woman of about twenty-five with a fair, narrow, diamond-shaped face — high cheekbones, a slim nose with a slightly upturned tip, wide-set grey eyes under fine, straight light brows, a narrow pointed chin and a small, full mouth; light auburn hair braided and coiled at the nape under a pearl fillet (not loose, no veil), and a composed, compassionate gaze.
cards.basis: Carpaccio's St. Anastasia in the Zadar polyptych, where her relics are kept: light auburn hair under a pearled fillet, a green gown, a dark mantle and a palm; the Orthodox icon gives the phial of the Pharmakolytria. Braiding the hair is an artistic choice to keep her apart from the long-haired virgin martyrs.
